text.en: Because a noun phrase fills one of the argument slots required by a verb, an independent noun phrase has an arity of -1 ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--because-a-noun-phrase-consumes-one-of-the⟧.
text.ja: 名詞句は動詞が要求する項スロットのひとつを占めるため、自立した名詞句のアリティは -1 である ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--because-a-noun-phrase-consumes-one-of-the⟧。

text.en: Nouns in Ainu are classified on morphosyntactic grounds into subclasses, with different scholars identifying slightly different inventories: Bugaeva recognises three major subclasses — common nouns, relational nouns, and bound nouns — while Nakagawa identifies four subclasses — common nouns, locative nouns, pronouns, and formal nouns — distinguished by five features: inflection, possessive case person affixes, independence, possible modifiers, and locativity ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-are-classified-on-morphosyntactic-grounds-into-three⟧⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--four-subcategories-of-nouns-can-be-identified-through⟧⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-nouns-are-classified-morphologically-and-affixally-into⟧. Bugaeva further distinguishes ordinary nouns from locative nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-has-a-nominal-classification-distinguishing-ordinary-nouns⟧, a distinction also recognised in Karafuto dialects, where many nouns in both classes have both a non-specific conceptual form and a specific, concrete affiliative form ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--karafuto-dialects-distinguish-ordinary-nouns-from-locative-nouns⟧. Both ordinary nouns and locative nouns change their forms through the attachment of suffixes to their basic forms ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--both-ordinary-nouns-and-locative-nouns-change-their⟧. Common nouns, long forms of positional nouns, and pronouns can independently serve as the subject or object of a verb ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--common-nouns-long-forms-of-positional-nouns-and⟧. Ainu nouns have no grammatical gender, only natural sex ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-in-ainu-have-no-grammatical-gender-only⟧. For animals, sexes are distinguished by prefixing *pinne* for male and *matne* for female ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--for-animals-sexes-are-distinguished-by-prefixing-pinne⟧. Just as *ainu* means 'human' in contrast to *kamui* but 'man' in contrast to *menoko*, the element *-kur* means 'male' in contrast to *-mat* ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--just-as-the-noun-ainu-means-human-in⟧; in Hidaka dialects, for instance, the words for male spider and female spider are *ka-erikin-kur* and *ka-erikin-mat* respectively ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-hidaka-the-words-for-male-spider-and⟧. In Sakhalin dialects, nouns placed after other nouns to qualify them, often expressing an indefinite plural, are called adnominal post-words and are also used as independent nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-placed-after-other-nouns-to-qualify-them⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の名詞は形態統語的性質に基づいて下位分類されるが、研究者によって認定される下位類の数は若干異なる。Bugaevaは普通名詞・関係名詞・所属名詞（結合名詞）の3大下位類を認め ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-are-classified-on-morphosyntactic-grounds-into-three⟧、中川は語形変化・所属格人称接辞・自立性・可能な修飾語・場所性の5つの特徴によって普通名詞・位置名詞・代名詞・形式名詞の4下位類を識別する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--four-subcategories-of-nouns-can-be-identified-through⟧⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-nouns-are-classified-morphologically-and-affixally-into⟧。Bugaevaはさらに普通名詞と位置名詞を区別し ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-has-a-nominal-classification-distinguishing-ordinary-nouns⟧、この区別は樺太方言でも認められ、両クラスの多くの名詞に非特定的な概念形と特定的・具象的な所属形の両方が存在する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--karafuto-dialects-distinguish-ordinary-nouns-from-locative-nouns⟧。普通名詞と位置名詞はともに、基本形に接尾辞が付加されることによって語形が変化する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--both-ordinary-nouns-and-locative-nouns-change-their⟧。普通名詞・位置名詞の長形・代名詞は単独で動詞の主語・目的語になることができる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--common-nouns-long-forms-of-positional-nouns-and⟧。アイヌ語の名詞には文法的性の現象はなく、自然の性のみが存在する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-in-ainu-have-no-grammatical-gender-only⟧。動物にあっては、雄に*pinne*、雌に*matne*を冠して区別する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--for-animals-sexes-are-distinguished-by-prefixing-pinne⟧。*ainu*という語が*kamui*に対して「人」を意味し*menoko*に対して「男」を意味するのと同様に、*-kur*も*-mat*に対しては「男性」を意味し ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--just-as-the-noun-ainu-means-human-in⟧、日高方言では雄蜘蛛と雌蜘蛛をそれぞれ*ka-erikin-kur*・*ka-erikin-mat*という ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-hidaka-the-words-for-male-spider-and⟧。樺太方言では、名詞に後置して不定複数を表す場合が多い語を連体後詞と呼び、独立した名詞としても使われる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nouns-placed-after-other-nouns-to-qualify-them⟧。

text.en: Ordinary nouns have two forms: the conceptual form and the affiliative form ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-ordinary-nouns-have-two-forms-the⟧. The conceptual form can constitute a noun phrase by itself and thus has an arity of -1, whereas the affiliative form requires an antecedent and thus has an arity of 0 ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-concept-form-of-a-common-noun-can⟧. All ordinary nouns have an underlying affiliative form that surfaces when semantic conditions such as a material-product relationship are met ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--all-ordinary-nouns-have-an-underlying-affiliative-form⟧. The conceptual form of ordinary nouns generally does not possess the syntactic function of 'location' ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-conceptual-form-of-ordinary-nouns-generally-does⟧. General nouns can function as sentence subject or object and may be followed by case postpositions ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-can-function-as-sentence-subject-or⟧; they are independent free forms that may perform the role of sentence subject by themselves ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-are-independent-free-forms-that-may⟧. General nouns may be preceded by adnouns and adnominalized sentences, and some may take noun suffixes and/or noun prefixes ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-may-be-preceded-by-adnouns-and⟧; only general nouns may be modified by adnouns or take noun prefixes, pronominal prefixes, or noun suffixes ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--only-general-nouns-may-be-modified-by-adnouns⟧. General nouns are unmarked for gender ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-are-unmarked-for-gender⟧. Quantity nouns can all appear in apposition to the noun they modify or function as pure nouns, but among them only *poronno* and *ponno* occur in adnominal position ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--quantity-nouns-can-all-appear-in-apposition-to⟧⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--among-quantity-nouns-only-poronno-and-ponno-occur⟧. The noun *topa* means 'group, flock, school, herd' and can be used for both animals and humans ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--topa-is-a-noun-meaning-group-flock-school⟧.
text.ja: 普通名詞には概念形と所属形の2つの形式がある ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-ordinary-nouns-have-two-forms-the⟧。概念形はそれ単独で名詞句を構成できるためアリティは -1 であるのに対し、所属形は先行詞を要求するためアリティは 0 である ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-concept-form-of-a-common-noun-can⟧。すべての普通名詞は基底において所属形を持つ性質があり、材料と製品の関係などの意味条件が満たされれば表面化する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--all-ordinary-nouns-have-an-underlying-affiliative-form⟧。普通名詞の概念形は一般に〈場所〉の統語的機能を持たない ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-conceptual-form-of-ordinary-nouns-generally-does⟧。普通名詞は文の主語または目的語になり得、格後置詞の後続を受けることができ ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-can-function-as-sentence-subject-or⟧、単独で文の主語の役割を果たすことができる独立した自由形式である ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-are-independent-free-forms-that-may⟧。普通名詞は連体詞や連体節の先行を受けることができ、一部は名詞接尾辞や名詞接頭辞を取り得る ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-may-be-preceded-by-adnouns-and⟧。連体詞によって修飾されたり、名詞接頭辞・人称接頭辞・名詞接尾辞を取ることができるのは普通名詞だけである ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--only-general-nouns-may-be-modified-by-adnouns⟧。普通名詞には文法的な性の標示がない ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--general-nouns-are-unmarked-for-gender⟧。数量名詞はすべて、修飾する名詞と同格になることも純粋な名詞として機能することもできるが、*poronno*と*ponno*だけが連体位でも現れる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--quantity-nouns-can-all-appear-in-apposition-to⟧⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--among-quantity-nouns-only-poronno-and-ponno-occur⟧。*topa*は「群れ」を意味する名詞であり、動物にも人間にも用いることができる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--topa-is-a-noun-meaning-group-flock-school⟧。

text.en: Bound nouns cannot occur independently and must be modified by a determiner, a noun, or a relative clause ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--bound-nouns-require-modification⟧. Obligatorily possessed nouns almost never occur without possessive morphology ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--obligatorily-possessed-nouns-almost-never-occur-without-possessive⟧; without an overt personal prefix, the default interpretation is that the possessor is third person ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--without-an-overt-personal-prefix-the-default-interpretation⟧. Ainu uses unspecified possessor and antipassive morphology as non-possessed noun morphology, allowing an obligatorily possessed noun to be used without a specified or overt possessor ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-uses-unspecified-possessor-and-antipassive-morphology-as⟧. Certain bound nouns, including *kur*, *utar*, *us(i)(ke)(he)*, *pe*/*p*, *hike*, and *hi*/*i*, occur more frequently as relative clause heads than common nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--certain-bound-nouns-including-kur-utar-us-i⟧. Ainu inalienable nouns include body part terms and their semantic extensions, including bodily secretions, physical strength, disposition, home, and clothing ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-inalienable-nouns-include-body-part-terms-and⟧; by contrast, *si*, *osoma* 'excrement', and *okuyma* 'urine' are encoded as alienably possessed nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-nouns-si-and-osoma-excrement-and-okuyma⟧. In riddles, obligatorily possessed nouns are cited with the fourth-person/first-person plural inclusive transitive subject prefix *a-* rather than in their conceptual form ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-riddles-obligatorily-possessed-nouns-are-cited-with⟧. Bound noun roots such as *me-* 'cold' and *mon-* 'hand' have an arity of -1 in the calculation of compound word arity, despite not being independent words ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--bound-noun-roots-such-as-me-cold-and⟧. The noun *ruye* or *ruyehe* only exists in the affiliative form ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-noun-ruye-or-ruyehe-only-exists-in⟧. In Sakhalin, nineteenth-century Japanese records preserve names of ethnic groups derived from the Ainu element *-kur*, meaning 'people' ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nineteenth-century-japanese-records-preserve-names-of-ethnic⟧.
text.ja: 所属名詞（結合名詞）は単独では生起できず、限定詞・名詞・関係節による修飾を必要とする ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--bound-nouns-require-modification⟧。義務的所有名詞は所有形態素を伴わずに現れることがほとんどなく ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--obligatorily-possessed-nouns-almost-never-occur-without-possessive⟧、人称接頭辞がない場合は所属主が三人称であるとデフォルトで解釈される ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--without-an-overt-personal-prefix-the-default-interpretation⟧。アイヌ語は不特定所有者および逆受動形態論を非所有名詞形態論として用い、義務的所有名詞を特定所有者や明示的な所有者なしで使用できるようにしている ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-uses-unspecified-possessor-and-antipassive-morphology-as⟧。*kur*・*utar*・*us(i)(ke)(he)*・*pe*/*p*・*hike*・*hi*/*i*などの結合名詞は、普通名詞よりも関係節主要部として高頻度で用いられる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--certain-bound-nouns-including-kur-utar-us-i⟧。アイヌ語の譲渡不能名詞には身体部位名詞および分泌物・体力・気質・住居・衣服などのその意味的拡張が含まれる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--ainu-inalienable-nouns-include-body-part-terms-and⟧が、*si*・*osoma*「糞」および*okuyma*「尿」は譲渡可能所有名詞として記号化される ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-nouns-si-and-osoma-excrement-and-okuyma⟧。謎々においては、義務的所有名詞は概念形ではなく一人称複数包括／四人称他動詞主語接頭辞*a-*を伴う所属形で用いられる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-riddles-obligatorily-possessed-nouns-are-cited-with⟧。*me-*「寒さ」や*mon-*「手」などの名詞語根は単独で単語にならないが、合成語のアリティ計算においてはアリティ -1 として扱われる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--bound-noun-roots-such-as-me-cold-and⟧。名詞*ruye*または*ruyehe*は所属形でのみ存在する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-noun-ruye-or-ruyehe-only-exists-in⟧。樺太では、19世紀の日本語記録に「人」を意味するアイヌ語要素*-kur*に由来する民族名が現れる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--nineteenth-century-japanese-records-preserve-names-of-ethnic⟧。

text.en: Kinship terms split into two grammatical classes with respect to possession. Some kinship terms, such as *unu-hu* 'his mother', *ona-ha* 'his father', *po-ho* 'child/son', and *sa-ha* 'his elder sister', are encoded as inalienable nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--some-kinship-terms-such-as-unu-hu-his⟧. Other kinship terms, including *totto* 'mother', *hapo* 'father/mother', *acapo* 'uncle', *unarpe* 'aunt', *huci* 'grandmother', and *ekasi* 'grandfather', are encoded as alienably possessed nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--kinship-terms-such-as-totto-mother-hapo-father⟧.
text.ja: 親族名称は所有の観点から2つの文法的クラスに分かれる。*unu-hu*「彼の母」・*ona-ha*「彼の父」・*po-ho*「子／息子」・*sa-ha*「彼の姉」などの一部の親族名称は譲渡不能名詞として扱われる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--some-kinship-terms-such-as-unu-hu-his⟧。一方、*totto*「母」・*hapo*「父／母」・*acapo*「叔父」・*unarpe*「叔母」・*huci*「祖母」・*ekasi*「祖父」などの親族名称は譲渡可能所有名詞として記号化される ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--kinship-terms-such-as-totto-mother-hapo-father⟧。

text.en: Locative nouns in Ainu have a basic form and long forms ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-in-ainu-have-a-basic-form⟧. Locational nouns express relative spatial relations such as 'above', 'below', 'front', and 'back', and are distinguished from common nouns by four properties: requiring a preceding reference noun in the basic form, forming long forms differently from affiliative forms, taking objective personal affixes, and always functioning syntactically as 'location' ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locational-nouns-express-relative-spatial-relations-like-above⟧. The basic form of a locational noun cannot form a noun phrase or sentence element on its own without a preceding noun that specifies its reference point ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-basic-form-short-form-of-a-locational⟧, and locative nouns are always treated syntactically as 'location' ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-are-always-treated-syntactically-as-location⟧.
text.ja: アイヌ語の位置名詞には基本形と長形がある ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-in-ainu-have-a-basic-form⟧。位置名詞は「上」「下」「前」「後」などの相対的位置関係を表し、短形では基準名詞を要求すること・所属形とは異なる方法で長形を作ること・目的格人称接辞を取れること・文法的に常に〈場所〉として扱われることの4つの特徴で普通名詞と区別される ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locational-nouns-express-relative-spatial-relations-like-above⟧。位置名詞の基本形は、基準点を示す先行名詞がなければ単独で名詞句をつくることも文の要素になることもできず ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--the-basic-form-short-form-of-a-locational⟧、位置名詞は統語的に常に〈場所〉として扱われる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-are-always-treated-syntactically-as-location⟧。

text.en: Locative nouns are divided into two types based on whether their basic forms require an antecedent noun phrase ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-are-divided-into-category-1-and⟧. Nakagawa proposes that Type 1 locational nouns cannot stand independently at sentence initial in their basic form, whereas Type 2 locational nouns can ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locational-nouns-are-divided-into-type-1-locational⟧. Type 1 locative nouns have an arity of 0 when preceded by an antecedent, and an arity of -1 when occurring without an antecedent in their long form, as with *ka*, *tum*, and *tom* ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--type-1-locative-nouns-have-an-arity-of⟧. Type 2 locative nouns likewise have an arity of 0 when an antecedent is present and an arity of -1 when no antecedent is present, as with *soy*, *rik*, and *wor* ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--type-2-locative-nouns-have-an-arity-of⟧.
text.ja: 位置名詞は基本形が先行名詞句を要求するかどうかに応じて2種に区分される ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locative-nouns-are-divided-into-category-1-and⟧。中川は、第一種位置名詞は基本形で単独で文頭に立てないのに対し、第二種位置名詞は基本形で自立語として文頭に立てると提案する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--locational-nouns-are-divided-into-type-1-locational⟧。第一種位置名詞は先行詞があればアリティは 0 であり、先行詞がなければ長形で -1 となり、*ka*・*tum*・*tom*などがこれにあたる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--type-1-locative-nouns-have-an-arity-of⟧。第二種位置名詞も先行詞があればアリティは 0 であり、先行詞がなければ -1 となり、*soy*・*rik*・*wor*などがこれにあたる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--type-2-locative-nouns-have-an-arity-of⟧。

text.en: Nakagawa asserts that in Ainu there is no grammatical distinction between proper nouns and common nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-there-is-no-grammatical-distinction-between⟧, while Refsing observes that proper names behave syntactically like general nouns but, unlike general nouns, never take plural suffixes ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-behave-syntactically-like-general-nouns-but⟧. Proper names are only in extremely rare cases modified by an adnoun or an adnominal clause ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-rarely-adnominally-modified⟧, and they can take no prefixes or suffixes ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-can-take-no-prefixes-or-suffixes⟧. In Hokkaido dialects, proper nouns do not take affiliative forms, whereas in Sakhalin dialects people's names possess affiliative forms ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-hokkaido-dialects-proper-nouns-do-not-take⟧. To avoid sharing names with others, Ainu personal names tended to be long, and most recorded names consist of two or more words, such as subject + verb or verb + noun ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--to-avoid-sharing-names-with-others-ainu-personal⟧. In Ainu, nicknames are called *pon re*, literally 'little name' ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-nicknames-are-called-pon-re-literally⟧. Names such as *Okikurmi* or *Samayunkur* in Hokkaido, and *Yayresuupo* or *Paarionnay* in Sakhalin, are considered proper nouns because each denotes a unique individual ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--names-of-beings-like-okikurmi-or-samayunkur-in⟧. Nakagawa proposes that in western Hokkaido heroic epics the protagonist *Poyyaunpe*, an epithet meaning 'young land person' that corresponds to a nickname (*pon re*), can be treated as a proper noun ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-western-hokkaido-heroic-epics-the-protagonist-poyyaunpe⟧. Nakagawa further proposes that expressions with the structure 'place name + *un* + *kur*/*mat*', such as *Iyoci un kur* or *Kanesanta un mat*, function within narratives as proper names denoting specific individuals rather than regional groups ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--expressions-with-the-structure-place-name-un-kur⟧.
text.ja: 中川はアイヌ語において普通名詞と固有名詞との間に文法的な差はないと主張する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-there-is-no-grammatical-distinction-between⟧が、Refsing は固有名詞が統語的には一般名詞と同様に振る舞うものの、一般名詞と異なり複数接尾辞をとることは決してないと述べる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-behave-syntactically-like-general-nouns-but⟧。固有名詞が連体詞や連体修飾節によって修飾されることは極めて稀であり ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-rarely-adnominally-modified⟧、接頭辞も接尾辞も取ることができない ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--proper-names-can-take-no-prefixes-or-suffixes⟧。北海道方言では固有名詞は所属形を持たないが、樺太方言では人名が所属形を持つ ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-hokkaido-dialects-proper-nouns-do-not-take⟧。似た名前になることを避けるためにアイヌ語の人名は必然的に長くなる傾向があり、記録されているアイヌ語の名前の多くは主語＋動詞・動詞＋名詞のように2語以上で成り立っているものが多い ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--to-avoid-sharing-names-with-others-ainu-personal⟧。アイヌ語であだ名は「小さな名」を意味する*pon re*と呼ばれる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-ainu-nicknames-are-called-pon-re-literally⟧。北海道の*Okikurmi*や*Samayunkur*、樺太の*Yayresuupo*や*Paarionnay*などの名は唯一の個体を指すため固有名詞の範疇に入れられる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--names-of-beings-like-okikurmi-or-samayunkur-in⟧。中川は、北海道西部の英雄叙事詩の主人公*Poyyaunpe*は「若い陸のやつ」という意味のあだ名（*pon re*）にあたるものであり固有名詞として扱ってよいと提案する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--in-western-hokkaido-heroic-epics-the-protagonist-poyyaunpe⟧。さらに中川は、*Iyoci un kur*や*Kanesanta un mat*のような「地名＋*un*＋*kur*/*mat*」という語構成の呼称は物語中では特定の個人を指すため固有名詞と見なすことができると提案する ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--expressions-with-the-structure-place-name-un-kur⟧。

text.en: Pronouns and formal nouns do not show inflectional changes in form, unlike common nouns ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--pronouns-and-formal-nouns-do-not-show-inflectional⟧. Pronouns other than personal pronouns, formal nouns, and bound nominal roots each have an arity of -1, as illustrated by forms such as *nep*, *tanpe*, *sinep*, *hi*, *p*, *pe*, *uske*, *me-*, and *nu-* ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--pronouns-other-than-personal-pronouns-formal-nouns-and⟧.
text.ja: 代名詞と形式名詞には普通名詞に見られるような語形変化がない ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--pronouns-and-formal-nouns-do-not-show-inflectional⟧。人称代名詞以外の代名詞・形式名詞・名詞語根はいずれもアリティが -1 であり、*nep*・*tanpe*・*sinep*・*hi*・*p*・*pe*・*uske*・*me-*・*nu-*などがその例として挙げられる ⟦claim:nominal/nominal-subclasses-and-bound-nouns--pronouns-other-than-personal-pronouns-formal-nouns-and⟧。
